question.prompt: What are the coordinates of the intersection of the lines \(y=x+1\) and \(y=-x+3\)?

solutions.explanation: Equating the two expressions gives \(x+1=-x+3\), so \(x=1\). Substitution gives \(y=2\), so the intersection is \((1,2)\).
solutions.title: Equate the two expressions for y

solutions.explanation:
At the intersection, both equations hold for the same \(x\) and \(y\). Their \(x\)-terms are opposites, so adding the equations eliminates \(x\):
\[
2y=(x+1)+(-x+3)=4.
\]
Thus \(y=2\). Substituting into \(y=x+1\) gives \(2=x+1\), so \(x=1\). The intersection is \((1,2)\).
solutions.title: Add to eliminate x
